title: Ansel and the Portrait
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Halloway is exhumed for a mausoleum renovation and found empty, night-shift taxi dispatcher Quentin Dravenmoor becomes an accidental witness: their dispatch logs show a cab carried a living, breathing man from the cemetery the night of the burial thirty years ago. Digging into faded ledgers and half-remembered fares, Quentin discovers that Edmund faked his death to escape a crime he didn't commit—and that someone in town has been paying ever since to keep the secret buried. As Quentin closes in on the identity of both the fugitive founder and his silent accomplice, they realize the empty coffin was reopened deliberately, as a message meant to flush Edmund's heir out of hiding. In the end, Quentin must choose between exposing a dead man who never died and protecting the fragile new life of the person who inherited his name.
about_author: B. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former small-town records clerk who spent years cataloguing other people's unfinished business. They write mysteries about the quiet crimes that settle into a place like sediment.

chapters.title: The Weight of Absence
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. During the mausoleum renovation, Quentin takes a routine call from the cemetery crew and learns Edmund Halloway's coffin holds nothing but river stones. The town reels while Quentin, professionally invisible, notices what no one else does: the exhumation date matches an odd entry in a thirty-year-old dispatch log. Emotional beat: unease—the thrill of being seen colliding with the fear of it.

chapters.title: Fares Paid in Silence
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Following the old log, Quentin finds the retired dispatcher who took a midnight fare from the cemetery gates in 1994—a man matching Edmund's description, alive. The dispatcher warns them off before dying quietly days later, ruled natural causes. Emotional beat: dread deepening into resolve, as Quentin realizes curiosity has made them a loose end.

chapters.title: The Heir Who Never Was
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Climax. Quentin traces the hush money through the Halloway estate to Marisol Halloway, Edmund's 'granddaughter,' who confesses: she is Edmund himself, living under an inherited identity, and the exhumation was staged by the true culprit's descendant to force him out. Confronted at the old depot, Quentin must decide whether to hand over the proof or burn it. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into moral clarity.

chapters.title: What the Stones Remember
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Resolution. Quentin gives the police only the log page naming the real killer—long dead—letting the living past stay buried. Edmund-as-Marisol leaves town on one last fare Quentin dispatches personally, a kindness between two people who know what it costs to be unseen. The coffin is resealed with stones, honestly this time. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; invisibility chosen, not imposed.
